wiki.note: The test wiki runs inside a Docker container with an extension checkout mounted over a Windows filesystem share. This shared-folder mount introduces substantial disk I/O and stat overhead for PHP file inclusion and asset loading, making measurements slower than a standard production Linux deployment.

PERF-1.charterTarget: A page with drawings gets at most 150 KB (gzip) of Layers code and styles; a page without drawings gets none.
PERF-1.notes: Met on test wiki. Measures only Layers' own ResourceLoader modules alone (gzip compressed); excludes core bundles.

PERF-2.charterTarget: A drawing appears within 300 ms after its image has loaded.
PERF-2.notes: Met on test wiki (drawing painted within 300 ms of photo load).

PERF-3.charterTarget: The editor is usable within 3 s of pressing Edit, with a warm cache.
PERF-3.notes: Met on test wiki (warm median < 3 s).

PERF-4.charterTarget: With 100 layers, dragging, resizing and panning run at 50 frames per second or more, and each typed character appears within 50 ms.
PERF-4.notes: Dragging runs at 60.5 FPS (>= 50 met); typing median is 48.55 ms (<= 50 met), but worst single-character latency was 50.1 ms (target: <= 50 ms).

PERF-5.charterTarget: Saving a 100-layer drawing takes at most 1 s on the server, and so does viewing an old revision.
PERF-5.notes: Not met on test wiki. Slower due to shared folder mount overhead; target applies to production reference install.

PERF-6.charterTarget: On a page with 20 drawings, drawings that are off screen are deferred, and no Layers task blocks the browser for more than 200 ms.
PERF-6.notes: Observed with type: 'longtask', buffered: true after waiting until all 20 drawings are confirmed painted.

PERF-7.charterTarget: A small edit to a drawing that contains images does not copy the image data into the new revision (see FEAT-3c).
PERF-7.notes: Criterion is not met: each edit re-serializes the entire drawing including the 200 KB image payload into the layers slot (slot size ~200 KB for both revisions), rather than storing only the delta (FEAT-3c).
